title: Burnside Counting — Prove rotatedIndex_add Composition Law

problemStatement.formal: \forall n,a,b,k\in\mathbb{N},\ 0<n\Rightarrow \operatorname{rotatedIndex}\ n\ a\ (\operatorname{rotatedIndex}\ n\ b\ k) = \operatorname{rotatedIndex}\ n\ ((a + b) \bmod n)\ k.
problemStatement.plain: Prove that rotating a necklace by one amount and then another is the same as rotating once by the combined amount modulo the necklace length.
whyMatters: This composition law is part of the cyclic group action used in the Burnside's lemma necklace-counting proof.
Formalizing it reduces reliance on ad hoc modular arithmetic assumptions around rotatedIndex.
The proof exercises the Mathlib modular arithmetic lemmas needed for the surrounding group-action infrastructure.

proven: The parent Burnside-counting gallery proof defines necklace rotation through rotatedIndex n a k = (k + a) % n.
Local notes identify the expected composition calculation as a Nat.add_mod-style modular arithmetic proof.
open: Confirm whether rotatedIndex_add is currently axiomatized, missing, or derivable directly in the Lean source.
Decide whether the needed statement is the direct composition law or the inverse variant using (a + n - b) % n.
knownResults.goal: Prove the rotatedIndex composition law needed for the Burnside necklace-counting rotation action.

currentState.focus: Locate the rotatedIndex definition and prove the modular composition law for necklace rotations.
currentState.nextAction: Inspect the BurnsideCounting Lean source, unfold rotatedIndex, and try Nat.add_mod/omega on the composition target.
